reason: I verified each change in the code, and every round-2 hole is closed. (1) ok now requires machine !== null and an APPROVED event whose reviewerId equals the reviewer:<id> in reviewedBy, so a non-prefixed name never passes. The name-over-machine canary ('Annie' over an agent-reviewer approval under rev-agent-01) would have passed under round 2 and is now caught. (2) The exclusion is id notIn [DRAFT_ID, LIVE_ID]. zz-e2e-fixture-word is no longer excluded; it is screened as seed. (3) A seed label is checked against the words.json ids plus the seed fixture id, and the read throws rather than returning empty (R173). The literal SEED_FIXTURE_WORD_ID matches seed.ts:393, and a rename there fails closed. The false-seed canary is caught, and the seed count is printed. (4) The approval must have at >= the last AUTHORED or AMENDED. The stale-approval canary (APPROVED t0, AMENDED t1) is caught. In the real V2 data, APPROVED and AMENDED tie to the millisecond on amend and rapid, written in the same landing, so >= is the correct comparison. (5) The digest canary strips gave-a-disgust's reviewNotes inside the rollback, asserts the clause fires, and asserts afterwards that cb80fc2f is restored. (6) The header carries no count. Earlier closures stand: every LIVE card is screened, the population is printed, an empty run fails, and self-approval is tested on event actors. The remaining notes are non-blocking.
holes: NON-BLOCKING. The R1051 'Raised, not fixed' paragraph now overstates the gap. It says an APPROVED event on an earlier version 'would still satisfy the test'. Since clause (4), that is true only of an edit written WITHOUT an AMENDED or AUTHORED event; a recorded edit after approval is caught. Reword so the register says exactly what the content-hash pin would add (R591).

NON-BLOCKING. The register-citation half of the exception clause has no canary. Only the digest half is exercised in the rollback; the citation half was proven once, historically, when the main test failed before R1051 existed. A canary exception entry pointing at a register id that does not cite it would keep it proven.

NON-BLOCKING. The seed check is by id, not content. A card labelled seed with a words.json id passes even if its text no longer matches words.json. That is reviewed-guard's territory (R62) rather than this door's, but the test's 'checked against what the seed writes' is true of the ids only.

NON-BLOCKING. Ties pass by design (>=). An AMENDED written in the same millisecond as, but after, an APPROVED is indistinguishable here. That is acceptable while both come from one lander transaction, and it is the content-hash pin's job to close.
